reason: Holds. CLC, LDA abs,X, BPL and ADC abs,X are all NMOS opcodes, so they are real on the 65SC12. LDA and BPL leave C alone, so C=0 reaches both ADC sfx_p_lo,X. .up is local to sfx_tick's braces and its only reference is BPL up. Cycles are the same on both paths (CLC 2 before the split, the per-path CLC 2 removed), so the saving is 1 byte. New layout: CLC &A4A0, LDA &A4A1, BPL &A4A4 (goes to &A4B2, same page), and ADC stays at &A4A6. From .up (&A4B3) the rest of bank 5's block moves down by 1. I scanned the listing to the end of the block: the sfx50 code, sfx_data, compiled_bank5 (ck1_*) and credits.6502 (1,199 instructions). Only 4 branches cross a page, and each crosses both before and after: BEQ ended, BCC credit_rts, BCC credit_end and BRA credit_end. compiled_bank5 has no indexed reads of tables in its own region and no branch that crosses a page. The indexed tables (sfx_* X 0-3 at &A5C6-&A5EE, credit_* X 0-1 at about &AFB2, sfx_effect_lo/hi - 1,Y with Y 1-8) cross no page either way. Self-modified operands (ramp+1/+2, nr_c1_b1..b5+2) are labels, so they move with their code and keep their meaning. Effect data: the ramp at &A5FD (offsets 1-5, 3 page crossings) moves to &A5FC (2 crossings), so it is 1 cycle faster and only rare. No ramp moves from &A600 to &A5FF. The sfx_ptr carry into the high byte is the same for every ramp. No slowdown found.
